A computed style is platform-neutral: colors, text styles, a border and
spacing. `ink_terminal_style()` adapts it to what a particular terminal can
show, and `ink_ansi_wrap()` serializes colors and text attributes as ANSI SGR
escape sequences. None of this requires a real terminal, and `inkr` does not
write to the terminal on its own.

```{r}
library(inkr)

sheet <- ink_compile(ink_parse("
  $accent: #7c3aed;

  Button.primary {
    color: white;
    background: $accent;
    text-style: bold;
    padding: 1 2;
    border: round $accent;
  }
"))
button <- ink_element("Button", classes = "primary")
computed <- ink_compute(sheet, button)
```

## Explicit capabilities

Capabilities are plain data that you supply. `inkr` never reads `TERM`,
`COLORTERM` or `NO_COLOR`; a host that wants detection performs it and passes
the result in.

```{r}
ink_terminal_capabilities(color_depth = "truecolor", unicode = TRUE)
ink_terminal_capabilities(color_depth = "ansi16", unicode = FALSE,
                          text_styles = c("bold", "underline"))
```

One computed style can be adapted for any number of capability profiles.

## Color depths

```{r}
for (depth in c("truecolor", "ansi256", "ansi16", "none")) {
  caps <- ink_terminal_capabilities(color_depth = depth)
  terminal <- ink_terminal_style(computed, caps)
  cat(sprintf("%-9s %s\n", depth, encodeString(ink_ansi_wrap("Save", terminal))))
}
```

Truecolor keeps RGB exactly. For `ansi256` an RGB color goes to the nearest
entry of the xterm color cube or grey ramp, and for `ansi16` to the nearest of
a fixed reference palette. Named ANSI colors stay ANSI colors at every depth,
which is why `white` is sent as `37`. With `"none"` no color instructions are
emitted.

## ANSI output

`ink_ansi_wrap(text, style, reset = TRUE)` returns the escape sequence, the
text and a reset. A style with nothing to apply returns the text unchanged.
Control characters in the text are removed, so untrusted text cannot inject
terminal commands.

```{r}
terminal <- ink_terminal_style(
  computed, ink_terminal_capabilities(color_depth = "truecolor")
)
styled <- ink_ansi_wrap("Save", terminal)
encodeString(styled)
encodeString(ink_ansi_wrap("Save", terminal, reset = FALSE))
encodeString(ink_ansi_wrap("bad\033[2Jtext", terminal))
```

To see the effect, a host would `cat(styled)` on an ANSI terminal.

## Borders and spacing metadata

Borders map to box-drawing characters (or ASCII when `unicode = FALSE`) and are
kept separate from the border color. Padding and margin are kept as
`c(top, right, bottom, left)` in cells. Nothing is drawn or measured.

```{r}
terminal
ascii <- ink_terminal_style(
  computed, ink_terminal_capabilities("ansi16", unicode = FALSE)
)
ascii
```

## Alpha compositing

Terminals have no alpha channel, so a partially transparent color is composited
onto a concrete RGB color before it is quantized:
`result = alpha * color + (1 - alpha) * underlying`. The underlying color is
the style's own opaque background or the explicit `matte` argument. If a color
needs compositing and no concrete background is known, the error
`unknown_alpha_background` is signalled; the terminal's real background is
never guessed.

```{r}
translucent <- ink_compute(
  ink_compile(ink_parse("Label { color: #ff000080; }")),
  ink_element("Label")
)
caps <- ink_terminal_capabilities(color_depth = "truecolor")
err <- tryCatch(ink_terminal_style(translucent, caps), ink_terminal_error = identity)
err$code
ink_terminal_style(translucent, caps, matte = "#000000")
```

## Styling versus rendering

`inkr` decides *what* an element looks like. It does not decide where it goes:
there is no layout engine, no text measurement or wrapping, no cursor control,
no input handling and no capability detection. The terminal style describes how
a style can be shown, and a host application, such as a TUI framework, is
responsible for drawing. Supported behavior is specified in
[docs/language-spec-v0.1.md](https://github.com/menshikovs/inkr/blob/main/docs/language-spec-v0.1.md);
see also `?ink_terminal_style`, `?ink_terminal_capabilities` and
`?ink_ansi_wrap`.
